month:1.gloss: The first month of the Gregorian calendar, following the December of the previous year and preceding February.

month:2.gloss: The short month following January and preceding March in the Roman, Julian, and Gregorian calendars, used in all three calendars for intercalation or addition o

month:3.gloss: The third month of the Gregorian calendar, following February and preceding April, containing the northward equinox.

month:4.gloss: The fourth month of the Gregorian calendar, following March and preceding May.

month:5.gloss: The fifth month of the Gregorian calendar, following April and preceding June.

month:6.gloss: The sixth month of the Gregorian calendar, following May and preceding July, containing the northern solstice.

month:7.gloss: The seventh month of the Gregorian calendar, following June and preceding August.

month:8.gloss: The eighth month of the Roman, Julian, and Gregorian calendars, following July and preceding September.

month:9.gloss: The ninth month of the Gregorian calendar, following August and preceding October, containing the southward equinox.

month:10.gloss: The tenth month of the Gregorian calendar, following September and preceding November.

month:11.gloss: The eleventh month of the Gregorian calendar, following October and preceding December.

month:12.gloss: The twelfth and last month of the Gregorian calendar, following November and preceding the January of the following year, containing the southern solstice.

weekday:1.gloss: The second day of the week in many religious traditions, and the first day of the week in systems using the ISO 8601 norm. It follows Sunday and precedes Tuesda

weekday:2.gloss: The third day of the week in many religious traditions, and the second day of the week in systems that use the ISO 8601 norm; it follows Monday and precedes Wed

weekday:3.gloss: The fourth day of the week in many religious traditions, and the third day of the week in systems using the ISO 8601 norm; it follows Tuesday and precedes Thurs

weekday:4.gloss: The fifth day of the week in many religious traditions, and the fourth day of the week in systems using the ISO 8601 norm; it follows Wednesday and precedes Fri

weekday:5.gloss: The sixth day of the week in many religious traditions, and the fifth day of the week in systems using the ISO 8601 norm; the Muslim Sabbath; it follows Thursda

weekday:6.gloss: The seventh day of the week in many religious traditions, and the sixth day of the week in systems using the ISO 8601 norm; the Jewish Sabbath; it follows Frida

weekday:7.gloss: The first day of the week in many religious traditions, and the seventh day of the week in systems using the ISO 8601 standard; the Christian Sabbath; it follow
